Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.


The workspace already contains at least two identical successful sampled rollouts, so I’m checking the full evidence set—not assuming the duplicate top-line score means duplicate dynamics. The shelf also requires its primitive catalog and source notes after metrics/keyframes are anchored.

The evidence set has three exact-score successful candidates at `0.173450` and one earlier successful baseline at `0.165860`; there is no failed sampled rollout in this workspace. I’ll therefore use the lower-scoring success as the “most informative failure-like” comparator and explicitly avoid claiming failure evidence that is not present.

The wake-visual skill now triggers the required image inspection. I’m reading the common held-fish wake first, then comparing the assigned parent’s released trajectory against the earlier `0.165860` trajectory before proposing any mechanism.

The sheets confirm both policies self-propel along the same diagonal wake-entry path; the parent reaches the target one frame-family earlier and avoids the comparator’s deeper terminal trough. That matches the `1.10`-time arrival gain and `389/3909` versus `439/4345` load reduction, so the next edit should preserve the base gait and near-target course damper rather than retune scalar propulsion.

The assigned parent also carries post-parent evaluation evidence: one-sided arbitration of opposing heading/course cues regressed to `45.331 / 1.72584L / 0.154397` with `413/4089` loads. I’ll distill that as a negative reusable boundary and inspect the sibling step-17 mechanism before choosing a genuinely new, compact test.

The sibling closure-scheduled course damper also regressed (`45.689 / 1.71923L / 0.161543`) while barely changing loads (`396/3917` versus `389/3909`). Together, the two step-17 outcomes argue against adding authority or cue arbitration inside the successful course residual. I’m checking their terminal sheets to verify that boundary visually.

The two degraded step-17 sheets retain the same wake-entry route but dip farther below the target, confirming that both extra course authority and heading/course arbitration disturb the validated terminal balance. I’m shifting the new test away from route-cue algebra: a bounded joint-rate-headroom allocator for the existing half-cycle steering residual, motivated by documented rate-cap contact and the shelf’s “preserve the rhythm, modulate the residual” invariant.

The shelf’s contribution is now concrete: it favors feedback modulation of a residual around an intact rhythmic gait. I’m recording the pre-edit diagnosis and falsifiable hypothesis first, as required; the candidate will leave the proven oscillator, route estimator, course damper, yaw gate, and posterior propulsion untouched.

The pre-edit notes are now in place. I’m applying the single mechanism exactly as recorded: separate smooth headroom gates on the two existing half-cycle residuals, with a candidate-owned nonzero floor; no route, propulsion, morphology, or environment changes.

The candidate and durable lesson are both updated. I’m invoking the mandated check-runner now for an independent contract audit; in parallel I’ll inspect the exact policy/guidance diffs for scope and semantic consistency.
